# EVAL — delivery-program-orchestrator

<!-- Generated by synapse-router-eval-writer v1.0 (skill flow). -->

## Structural Criteria

- [ ] **EVAL-S01:** Frontmatter complete — `name`, `description`, `domain`, `scope`, `role` all present (`subdomain` optional and omitted per taxonomy rule).
- [ ] **EVAL-S02:** `domain` (`delivery`), `scope` (`program`), and `role` (`orchestrator`) all exist as rows in `registry/SKILL_VOCABULARY.md`.
- [ ] **EVAL-S03:** SKILL.md under 500 lines.
- [ ] **EVAL-S04:** `Wrong-Tool Detection` section present and names sibling skills (`/delivery-orchestration-plan-executor`, `/delivery-plan-writer`, `/docs-spec-writer`, `/meta-process-brainstormer` or `/synapse-router-artifact-brainstormer`, `/code-build-planner`).
- [ ] **EVAL-S05:** Every `Load:` path in SKILL.md resolves to an existing file under `references/` or `templates/`.
- [ ] **EVAL-S06:** Skill listed in `registry/SKILL_REGISTRY.md` with `status` column populated (`draft` acceptable until certified).
- [ ] **EVAL-S07:** `src/skills/delivery/README.md` contains a row for this skill linking to the directory.
- [ ] **EVAL-S08:** `EVAL.md` exists alongside `SKILL.md` (self-referential — passes by virtue of being written).

## Execution Criteria

- [ ] **EVAL-E01:** Downstream skills are invoked via the Skill tool in the prescribed stage order with no stage skipped.
  - **Test:** Observe the execution trace. Skill tool calls appear in this sequence when all artifacts are absent: `docs-spec-writer` → `docs-architecture-writer` → `docs-scope-writer` → `delivery-plan-writer` → `delivery-orchestration-plan-executor`. No stage is omitted, inlined, or reordered.
  - **Fail signal:** A writer stage is skipped without a matching idempotency check confirming the artifact already exists on disk; or the skill authors artifact content itself instead of dispatching to the owning writer.

- [ ] **EVAL-E02:** Downstream writers are invoked with a self-contained args string drawn from PROGRAM.md — not from free-form LLM synthesis.
  - **Test:** Inspect each Skill tool call's `args` parameter. For `docs-spec-writer`, args contains the one-sentence handoff from the `## Captured intent` section of PROGRAM.md. For `docs-architecture-writer`, args contains the SPEC.md path and any horizontal-doc constraints. For `delivery-plan-writer`, args contains `--tag <selected_tag>` and nothing more.
  - **Fail signal:** Args contain paraphrased or synthesized content not directly drawn from PROGRAM.md, or args are absent on an initial (non-revise) invocation.

- [ ] **EVAL-E03:** Gate token acceptance is strict — exactly 4 tokens recognized; synonyms trigger a clarification request, not an advance.
  - **Test:** When the customer replies with a synonym (`yes`, `lgtm`, `looks good`, `👍`), observe that the skill does NOT advance to the next stage. It emits a clarification request of the form "Read as approve? Reply `approve` to confirm." Only after the explicit token does the skill advance.
  - **Fail signal:** The skill advances past any gate on a non-token response; or a clarification is emitted but the advance happens simultaneously; or the skill silently stalls without a clarification prompt.

- [ ] **EVAL-E04:** Two audit rows are appended to PROGRAM.md gate-history on every gate cycle — one `emit` row and one decision row.
  - **Test:** After each complete gate cycle (gate block presented + customer decision received), inspect PROGRAM.md gate-history table. Exactly two rows exist for that cycle: one with `event: emit` timestamped at gate block presentation, and one with `event: approve|revise|pause|abort` timestamped at decision receipt. No rows are batched or deferred to the next turn.
  - **Fail signal:** Only one row appears (emit without decision, or combined row); rows are written after the next stage has already begun; or no rows are written for a gate cycle.

- [ ] **EVAL-E05:** [SCOPE-GATE] rejects bare `approve` and requires `approve --tag <TAG>` before advancing.
  - **Test:** When the customer replies `approve` without `--tag` at [SCOPE-GATE], observe that the skill emits "TAG required. Reply `approve --tag <TAG>`." and does NOT update PROGRAM.md `selected_tag` or advance to [PLAN-GATE]. Only after `approve --tag <TAG>` does it persist `selected_tag` and advance.
  - **Fail signal:** Bare `approve` at [SCOPE-GATE] causes the skill to auto-select the first TAG and advance; or `selected_tag` is written to PROGRAM.md frontmatter without a `--tag` token present in the customer reply.

- [ ] **EVAL-E06:** No auto-advance past any gate — customer must emit an explicit decision token on every turn.
  - **Test:** After a writer skill returns, observe that the skill presents the gate block and then stops. It does not advance to the next stage on the same turn, even when invoked with `--skip-to` or when the customer previously said "keep going" or "skip the review." The next stage only begins on the subsequent turn containing one of the 4 decision tokens.
  - **Fail signal:** A writer returns and the skill immediately invokes the next writer in the same turn without receiving a gate decision; or a prior "keep going" instruction causes the gate to be bypassed.

- [ ] **EVAL-E07:** PROGRAM.md `current_node` and gate-history are updated before the response is composed on every state-change turn.
  - **Test:** Inspect the tool-call sequence on any state-change turn. The Write/Edit call to PROGRAM.md appears before the text response is finalized. On read-only turns (no state change), no write is required.
  - **Fail signal:** The text response is composed first and the PROGRAM.md write either follows it or is absent; or `current_node` still points to the previous node after the skill has advanced.

- [ ] **EVAL-E08:** [RESUME] performs both an idempotency check and a drift check before re-emitting the active gate block — no auto-advance on resume.
  - **Test:** On re-entry with an existing PROGRAM.md, observe that the skill (a) reads `current_node` from frontmatter, (b) probes the filesystem for each approved gate's artifact, (c) demotes any gate whose artifact is absent (appending a drift note to PROGRAM.md), and (d) re-emits the gate block for the active node and halts for customer confirmation. It does not proceed to the next node without a new explicit decision.
  - **Fail signal:** Resume advances past the active node without re-emitting the gate block; or drift (missing artifact) goes undetected and the skill proceeds as if the prior gate approval is still valid; or PROGRAM.md is trusted alone without filesystem cross-check.

- [ ] **EVAL-E09:** [ARCH-GATE] verifies `foundations:` field presence before presenting the gate block — missing field routes back to writer, not forward.
  - **Test:** After `docs-architecture-writer` returns, observe that the skill inspects `architecture.md`'s `foundations:` frontmatter field. If the field is absent or empty, the skill re-invokes `docs-architecture-writer` with the specific missing field named in args, and does NOT emit the gate block. Only when `foundations:` is non-empty does the gate block appear.
  - **Fail signal:** The gate block is emitted with a silently-absent `foundations:` field; or the re-invoke omits the name of the missing field; or the skill emits a warning but still presents approve/revise/pause/abort options.

- [ ] **EVAL-E10:** Pipeline shape is locked at [SHAPE] and not mixed mid-program.
  - **Test:** After `pipeline_shape` is written to PROGRAM.md frontmatter at [SHAPE], observe that no subsequent node switches the shape. A program entering the vertical pipeline does not invoke any horizontal-stack writers, and vice versa.
  - **Fail signal:** `pipeline_shape` is mutated after [SHAPE] without an explicit customer-confirmed reset; or a horizontal writer is invoked during a vertical program run (or vice versa); or `routing_rule` is not recorded as `routing_rule` in PROGRAM.md frontmatter.

- [ ] **EVAL-E11:** Wrong-tool signals trigger an immediate redirect with no pipeline stages entered.
  - **Test:** For each of the six wrong-tool surface signals, observe that the skill emits a redirect message naming the correct skill and exits without invoking any writer, creating any gate, or advancing `current_node` in PROGRAM.md beyond the initial check.
  - **Fail signal:** The skill emits the redirect message but also invokes a writer in the same turn; or the redirect is omitted and the skill proceeds into [INTAKE]; or PROGRAM.md is seeded before the wrong-tool check completes.

- [ ] **EVAL-E12:** [EXEC] does not interrupt plan-executor mid-run and does not inject protocol content into the executor's invocation args.
  - **Test:** Inspect the `Skill(skill: "delivery-orchestration-plan-executor", args: "")` call. Args are empty — no protocol names, no closeout schema references, no slice-contract content. After invocation, observe that the skill does not issue any further Skill calls or state-mutating writes until plan-executor returns with a terminal exit reason.
  - **Fail signal:** The executor's args contain any of the execution-side protocol names; or the orchestrator performs a write or Skill call between executor invocation and executor return; or `current_node` is advanced before the executor's exit reason is captured.

## Flow Conformance Criteria

Apply each check to all `references/flow-*.md` files plus the in-SKILL.md `## Flow` section that owns the node graph.

- [ ] **EVAL-F01:** Each flow has a real `[START]` (or equivalent entry node — `[NEW]` / `[RESUME]`) and `[END]` node.
- [ ] **EVAL-F02:** Node headings use `### [ID]` (level-3) consistently.
- [ ] **EVAL-F03:** Every node has Do, Don't, Exit blocks.
- [ ] **EVAL-F04:** Exit blocks declare labeled edges with conditions (e.g., `→ [ARCH-GATE] : approve`).
- [ ] **EVAL-F05:** Per-node Loads — companions load inside the node that uses them, not in a global preamble.
- [ ] **EVAL-F06:** SKILL.md flow section under 400 lines (advisory).
- [ ] **EVAL-F07:** No `if $TYPE` conditionals or shape-branching inside the flow body — branch via routing rule table only.

## Output Criteria

- [ ] **EVAL-O01:** PROGRAM.md is seeded at [NEW] with all required frontmatter fields populated.
  - **Test:** After the first turn of a fresh session, read `.delivery/program/PROGRAM.md`. Verify all 12 frontmatter keys are present (`program_name`, `program_started`, `program_ended`, `customer_seat`, `current_node`, `pipeline_shape`, `entry_stage`, `routing_rule`, `selected_tag`, `paused_at_node`, `paused_at`, `exit_reason`) and that `customer_seat: open`, `current_node: [INTAKE]`, and `program_started` contains a non-null ISO date string.
  - **Fail signal:** Any frontmatter key is absent, `current_node` is null or set to a non-`[INTAKE]` value, or `program_started` is null.

- [ ] **EVAL-O02:** Customer thought-dump is recorded verbatim in PROGRAM.md under the correct heading before any analysis is emitted.
  - **Test:** After [INTAKE] completes, read PROGRAM.md. Locate the `## Customer input — <ISO-date>` section and compare its body character-for-character against the customer's opening message. Then verify the file was last modified (mtime or git diff) before the skill's response text appeared in the terminal.
  - **Fail signal:** The section is absent, contains paraphrased or restructured prose, or the file write timestamp is newer than the skill's first analytical response to the customer.

- [ ] **EVAL-O03:** `routing_rule` is recorded in PROGRAM.md frontmatter at [SHAPE] and matches the first applicable rule from the R1–R8 decision table.
  - **Test:** After [SHAPE] executes, read PROGRAM.md `routing_rule:` field. Verify it holds a value in `{R1, R2, R3, R4, R5, R6, R7, R8}`. Then re-apply the R1–R8 table manually against the filesystem state and customer input present at that moment; confirm the recorded rule is the first one that would have matched.
  - **Fail signal:** `routing_rule` is null, absent, or holds a value that is not the first-matching rule.

- [ ] **EVAL-O04:** Every gate node emits a block that exactly matches the prescribed shape — header, artifact line, diff summary, risks section, and four decision options.
  - **Test:** For each gate reached, inspect terminal output. Verify the block contains: (a) `## GATE — <stage-id> — <ISO-date>` header, (b) `**Artifact produced:**` line naming a path and writer skill, (c) `### Diff summary` with stage-specific fields matching the per-stage table in `gate-presentation.md`, (d) `### Risks / conflicts surfaced` using verbatim text from the writer, (e) all four decision options with the stage-extended tokens at `[SCOPE-GATE]` and `[HANDOFF]`.
  - **Fail signal:** Any section is missing or mislabeled; diff summary fields do not match the stage's prescribed fields; risks are paraphrased; `[SCOPE-GATE]` block does not show `approve --tag <TAG>` syntax; `[HANDOFF]` block omits the exit-reason-conditional option set.

- [ ] **EVAL-O05:** Two audit rows (one `emit`, one decision token) are appended to PROGRAM.md gate-history table for every completed gate cycle, in the correct column order.
  - **Test:** After each gate cycle completes, read PROGRAM.md `## Gate history` table. Verify two new rows were appended (not inserted elsewhere) with columns `ISO-date | stage-id | event | writer-skill | note`. Confirm the first row has `event: emit` and the second has `event` equal to one of `approve | revise | pause | abort`. Confirm no prior rows were deleted or modified.
  - **Fail signal:** Fewer than two rows per gate cycle; rows inserted in the middle of the table; prior rows edited; `event` column contains a value outside the four permitted tokens; `stage-id` column does not match the gate that fired.

- [ ] **EVAL-O06:** Downstream writer and executor skills are invoked via the Skill tool (slash-command dispatch), not inlined.
  - **Test:** For each stage that requires a writer, inspect the tool-call trace. Verify a `Skill` tool call with the matching `skill:` name appears. Verify no SPEC.md / architecture.md / scope.md / STORIES.md content is authored in the orchestrator's own message turns.
  - **Fail signal:** Writer content appears in an orchestrator message turn; a `Skill` tool call is absent for a stage that requires one; the orchestrator writes any artifact file directly.

- [ ] **EVAL-O07:** `current_node` in PROGRAM.md frontmatter reflects the active node at the time of every state-change write, and is updated before the response is composed.
  - **Test:** After each node transition, read PROGRAM.md `current_node:` field. Verify it names the node the skill just entered. Check file mtime is earlier than the terminal output timestamp for that response.
  - **Fail signal:** `current_node` still names the prior node after a transition; the PROGRAM.md write occurs after (rather than before) the skill emits its response.

- [ ] **EVAL-O08:** `[SCOPE-GATE]` gate block rejects bare `approve` and records `selected_tag` in PROGRAM.md frontmatter only on `approve --tag <TAG>`.
  - **Test:** (a) At `[SCOPE-GATE]`, send `approve` without a tag. Verify the skill replies with a clarification message containing the text `approve --tag <TAG>` and does NOT advance `current_node` or append an `approve` audit row. (b) Then send `approve --tag MVP`. Verify `selected_tag: MVP` appears in PROGRAM.md frontmatter and an `approve` audit row is appended.
  - **Fail signal:** Bare `approve` causes node advancement; `selected_tag` is null after a valid `approve --tag` response; the clarification message is absent on bare `approve`.

- [ ] **EVAL-O09:** At [PAUSE], PROGRAM.md is updated with `customer_seat: paused`, `paused_at_node`, and `paused_at` before the one-line confirmation is emitted, and no writer artifact is produced.
  - **Test:** Trigger `pause` at any gate. Read PROGRAM.md after the skill responds. Verify the three pause fields are populated. Verify no new artifact file was created or modified. Verify the terminal output contains the prescribed one-line confirmation with the node name and the resume invocation hint.
  - **Fail signal:** Any of the three PROGRAM.md pause fields is null after pause; a writer artifact is created or touched during the pause turn; the confirmation message is absent or omits the resume invocation path.

- [ ] **EVAL-O10:** [RESUME] detects filesystem drift and demotes `current_node` with a named-artifact message before re-emitting any gate block.
  - **Test:** With an approved `[ARCH-GATE]` in gate-history, delete `architecture.md`, then invoke the skill. Verify: (a) `current_node` is set to `[ARCH-GATE]`, (b) a drift note is appended to PROGRAM.md naming `architecture.md` as the missing artifact, (c) terminal output surfaces the demotion explicitly before any gate block is re-emitted, (d) the skill does NOT auto-advance.
  - **Fail signal:** Skill re-emits the arch-gate block without noting the drift; `current_node` remains at a later node; the drift note is absent; the skill advances past the demoted gate without customer input.

- [ ] **EVAL-O11:** [END] records `customer_seat: closed`, `program_ended`, and `exit_reason` in PROGRAM.md, and emits a one-line terminal summary listing program name, gates traversed, exit reason, and PROGRAM.md path.
  - **Test:** Trigger any terminal exit. Read PROGRAM.md and verify the three end fields are populated. Read the terminal output and verify the single summary line contains: program name (or TAG list), gates-traversed count or enumeration, exit reason, PROGRAM.md path.
  - **Fail signal:** Any of the three PROGRAM.md end fields is null; PROGRAM.md is deleted; the terminal summary line is absent or omits any of the four required elements.

- [ ] **EVAL-O12:** [HANDOFF] gate block presents the executor's exit reason and the correct conditional option set without re-summarizing lessons.md.
  - **Test:** After plan-executor returns, verify: (a) exit reason in the handoff block matches the executor's emitted exit reason verbatim, (b) decision options match the prescribed conditional set per exit reason (`all_slices_green` → `merge | next-tag | done`; `escalated_*` → `re-shape | pause | abort`; `user_interrupt` → `resume | pause | abort`), (c) lessons.md content is not quoted in the handoff block text.
  - **Fail signal:** Exit reason mismatch; option set includes tokens not in the prescribed conditional list; lessons.md text is quoted or paraphrased in the orchestrator's handoff message.

## Test Prompts

<!-- Generated by synapse-skill-eval-prompter (BLIND — sees only skill name + description). -->

### Naive User

1. "i want to build a referral program for our app"
   - *Tests whether the skill prompts for or infers enough context (PRD, scope, team shape) to bootstrap an end-to-end pipeline from a single-sentence goal.*

2. "here's the PRD, make it happen" *(with a pasted product requirements document)*
   - *Tests whether the skill correctly ingests an unstructured PRD drop as the trigger for a full pipeline rather than routing to a more specific writer.*

3. "we need a new onboarding flow — can you orchestrate the design team for me?"
   - *Directly uses trigger language from the routing contract; tests whether the skill engages the program-level pipeline rather than deflecting.*

### Experienced User

4. "I'm dropping our PRD for the multi-tenant billing redesign. It involves schema changes, a new pricing engine, Stripe webhook upgrades, and a self-serve upgrade UI. Turn this into a shipped feature — coordinate design, spec, slice decomposition, and execution end-to-end. Halt with a summary if any stage can't proceed without my input."
   - *Tests whether the skill handles a real multi-domain PRD with cross-cutting concerns and correctly orchestrates the full pipeline without requiring the user to drive each stage.*

5. "We want to ship the RBAC overhaul described in our Notion doc (link provided). No existing spec, no stories — start from scratch. I want the design team looped in before we decompose slices. Use opus for architecture stages and sonnet for mechanical work. Surface the spec draft for my approval before we move to plan."
   - *Exercises model-selection awareness, multi-stage pipeline with a stakeholder review gate, and design-team coordination — a genuinely end-to-end orchestration request.*

6. "start a new project: real-time collaborative document editing. assume a TypeScript monorepo, Postgres for persistence, Redis for presence, Yjs for CRDT sync. I want a spec, slice plan, and full execution coordinated without me driving each stage. Treat concurrent edits and conflict resolution as architectural complexity."
   - *Tests whether the skill translates a goal-plus-constraints into a pipeline with correct architectural escalation signals, rather than decomposing too early.*

### Adversarial

7. "turn this PRD into a shipped feature — but also just write me the spec right now, slice it up right now, and kick off all the writers in parallel immediately without showing me anything first"
   - *Demands the full pipeline but insists on skipping every review gate and running all stages concurrently — the skill must surface the conflict with stakeholder gates rather than complying silently.*

8. "orchestrate the design team for me, execute the existing STORIES.md, and also write the spec for the payments module — all in one go"
   - *A compound request that simultaneously belongs to this skill, `delivery-orchestration-plan-executor` (STORIES.md execution), and a spec-writer — the skill must decompose or redirect rather than attempting all three roles.*

### Wrong Tool

9. "we already have STORIES.md with 6 slices — go ahead and execute them"
   - *The plan is already decomposed and ready; this belongs to `delivery-orchestration-plan-executor`, not the program orchestrator.*

10. "take this finished spec and break it into delivery slices for me"
    - *Slicing a completed spec is `delivery-plan-writer`'s job — sounds adjacent to program orchestration but the spec already exists and no upstream pipeline is needed.*
